priority.override_reason: The exact rank-one HashMap, rank-three public-field Raytrace, and rank-six CDJS profiles remain distributed across generic dispatch, direct-call/frame setup, Value lifetime, and named-property work; their individually bounded dispatch/frame leaves have just failed T026-T028 at roughly 1.6 percent payoff despite mechanism coverage. Rank-two date formatting, rank-four Tagcloud, rank-five binary trees, and the intervening RegExp, string, constructor, helper-graph, typed-loop, cache, and object-storage mechanisms are likewise closed by current negative evidence. Rank-fifteen access-nbody exposes a different stable representation cost: 310 of 3,660 current samples are platform string comparison while repeated named reads and writes use seven static Body fields. A prior pointer-only comparison failed because each bytecode site owned a different Rc<str>; this unit changes that premise by sharing static property-name identity across one complete compilation graph, while retaining content equality across separately compiled code.

mechanism.summary: Intern static named-property keys once per compilation graph, share that table with every nested-function compiler and any capture-recompilation pass, and let named Small-property reads, slot resolution, and writes accept pointer identity before falling back to textual equality.
mechanism.generality: Every script, module, eval body, Function body, and internally compiled body receives an independent compilation-local table. A root compiler and every nested compiler it creates share only equal static property names from that compilation graph; no workload name, source path, function name, property spelling, input, iteration count, checksum, or expected result controls admission. Object storage and named bytecode retain Rc<str> and their existing textual fallback, so separately compiled code, dynamic computed strings, cross-realm objects, eval, and Function-constructor results remain interoperable without global mutable state or a public representation change.
semantic_risks: a nested function compiled once or recompiled after lexical-capture discovery must use the same interner as its root and siblings rather than silently creating a second identity domain
separately compiled scripts, direct eval, modules, Function bodies, and cross-realm accesses must continue to match equal property text even when their Rc identities differ
pointer equality may bypass textual comparison only for byte-equal immutable Rc<str> values; computed property-key coercion, Symbols, private names, and array-index semantics remain unchanged
named reads and writes must preserve accessor, Proxy, prototype, descriptor, extensibility, strict-error, cache-invalidation, and insertion-order behavior on both identity hits and textual fallbacks
the compile-time table must not survive as mutable realm-global state or keep unrelated source graphs alive

profile_evidence.shared_cost: The successful 3,660-sample main-thread profile records 276 flat samples in _platform_memcmp and 34 in its executable stub: 8.47 percent directly in string comparison. The same run separately records 134 samples in existing-own-data writes, 121 in shared-slot reads, 72 in shared-slot resolution, 52 in typed-loop writeback, and further named-cache/read/write frames. Body objects repeatedly use the same seven static field spellings across constructors, methods, and the typed loop, but those sites currently carry separately allocated Rc<str> values, so Small storage falls through to byte comparison.
